To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ultimate attainment in interlanguage grammar is constrained by prosodic representations and that these representations can be minimally adapted.
the ultimate attainment in the interlanguage grammar of Mandarin speakers of English is constrained by their prosodic representations in Mandarin, which can be minimally adapted in the L2.
Mandarin-speaking learners of English can acquire target-like tense and participial inflection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how do speakers of languages with different morphological structures acquire a new language?
the question of what the L2 learner can achieve, and what the L1 learner cannot.
the acquisition of functional categories in L2, and the role of prosodic representations in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ultimate attainment in interlanguage grammar is not constrained by the L1 grammar, but by the L1 phonology.
the L2 learners’ grammatical representations can be more flexible than previously thought, but that this does not mean that L2 acquisition is not constrained in any way.
the L1 prosodic representation is the main factor that determines the ultimate attainment in interlanguage grammar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L2 acquisition is constrained by L2 transfer, but that L2 transfer is constrained by the L1 prosodic system.
the prosodic structure of the L1 is the most important factor in L2 acquisition, and that the L1 prosodic structure is a crucial factor in the ultimate attainment of the L2.
the ultimate attainment in interlanguage grammar is not limited to the representational capacity, which is constrained by the first language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L2 acquisition is not necessarily constrained by the representational limitations of the L1.

L2 speakers can acquire target-like prosodic structures even when the target language is not available to them as a native speaker, and that the L2 learner can build such structures by recombining the prosodic elements that are available in the L1.
prosodic transfer can be used to account for the ultimate attainment of functional categories in L2 grammars.
